- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) or neutral, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–2% to account for mean reversion.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model overreacts and forecasts continued rise; cap forecast at 1–2% above peak or adjust downward if sentiment turns negative.
- Model consistently underestimates early in 30-day horizon; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast for first 5–7 days if sentiment is positive.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model fails to capture mean reversion; apply smoothing filter to reduce volatility in forecast.
- When sentiment is flat or negative for 3+ consecutive days, model often ignores downward trend; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.
